description: The eng-tools developers maintain eqsig, a Python package for processing recorded and experimental earthquake-engineering signals. The repository documents response spectra, time-history processing and signal measures used to characterise shaking. Users supply acceleration or other measured time series and choose processing settings; outputs are calculated motion measures and plots for the selected event and station. Its geographic coverage depends on the input records, not a bundled regional database. The README links package installation and documentation, and GitHub metadata states the MIT licence. A limitation is that an intensity measure cannot represent all structural damage processes; records need unit checks, baseline correction and site-context review before use. eqsig can prepare seismic inputs and compare simulated responses with measured shaking for buildings or bridges. The related catalogue OpenSees model is a structural solver, while eqsig prepares signals; no tested interface between them is claimed. No ground-motion files or package were downloaded.
